description.narrative: Insatsens övergripande mål är att stöda unga från låg- och medelinkomstländer att delta i diskussionerna inför, under och efter Stockholm+50, samt att stärka ungas kapacitet och kunskap för att kunna ta en större plats i framtida internationella dialoger om globala frågor. Insatsen görs i samarbete mellan LSU och Stockholm+50 Youth Task Force.

The contributions overarching goal is to support Low- to middle income country (LMIC) youth in participating in discussions leading up to, during and after Stockholm+50, as well as strengthening LMIC youth capacity and knowledge to be able to take a more central role in future international dialogues on global issues. The contribution is a collaboration between LSU and the Stockholm+50 Youth Task Force.

The intervention aims to enhance and enable the meaningfully and equal participation by youth from low- and middle income countries (LMIC) in the processes for engagement leading up to, during and after the Stockholm50 conference in Stockholm in 2nd-3rd of June 2022. The intervention is looking to support LMIC youth in increasing their capabilities to paticipate in an meaningful way by hosting consultations leading up to the conference, as well as directly enabling the participation of LMIC youth at the conference itself and in side events.
LSU with partners is also looking to ensure the retention and advancement of LMIC youth's needs, ideas and demands in the aftermath of Stockholm50 based on the supported modes of engagement. They will also seek to strengthen the capacity and understanding between youth actors and decision makers in how to create meaningful youth participation in multilateral dialogues and conferences.

Despite a very short time frame, LSU and partners managed to organize capacity building events for youth in or from LMIC, consultation processes with LMIC youths and direct support for individual participation in the main S50 meeting for selected youth representatives from LMIC. However, the time frame did clearly limit the amount of activities they managed to carry out which they do reflect upon in the final report.
The main capacity building activities were sessions and workshops held in the beginning of local consultations, during the Youth Environmental Assembly pre-meetings prior to S50 as well as a Toolkit and Education pack for local level capacity building. Both the evaluator and the project team perceived the capacity building activities to have successfully supported LMIC youth to actively engage with the general participatory processes for youth in relation to S50.
The evaluation highlighted that the organizers clearly planned for inclusive and non-discriminatory processes for consultations and the drafting of the Youth policy paper. The main limitation was in terms of outreach as there was not enough time, resources and staff to do widespread and far reaching outreach. The intervention was also limited by language barriers, access to internet, and denied Visas for Sweden (which disproportionally hindered youth from LMIC).
Some LMIC youth representatives funded by the intervention did get Visas and were able to take part in the S50 main event as well as the Youth Environmental Assembly pre-meeting. Due to this, the contribution directly supported voices of LMIC youth at S50 that would potentially not have been present without this support. Assuming these participants would otherwise not have been present att the event, the contribution can be seen to have increased the power and voice of LMIC youth in relation to this meeting.
The perhaps strongest tangible result of the work with youth inclusion as a whole was the emphasis on the Youth policy paper in the final outcome document of the S50 meeting. The Sida funded contribution increased the involvement of LMIC youth in the process of deriving the Youth policy paper and thus strengthened it as a vehicle of power and voice for LMIC youths. This being said, it is very hard to ascertain how much the contribution increased the influence LMIC youth perspectives in the final document as it was an open process where great many inputs were combined and summarized.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
